rationale: The DECLARED half of the `?` decision, and the reason the wildcard half lives in a separate fixture. `class ?` and `type ?[A]` are legal Scala 3 (test/files/neg/qmark-deprecated.scala:9,22 publish both as real symbols), so a blanket 'suppress a `?` type name' rule would delete true edges — measured: 16 `references -> ?` endpoints on the corpus come from files that DO declare `?`, against the 49 that do not. The guard is therefore per-file. Without this fixture the narrow guard is indistinguishable from the blanket one that loses the 16.

expectRelationships.note: `type `?`[A]` is declared in THIS file, so `def useQmark(x: ?[Int])` references a real type name and the edge must stay — the false-positive half of the per-file rule
